title: Maximal Rényi Relative Entropy for $α>2$
abstract: Quantum relative entropies play a fundamental role in quantum information theory. In the classical setting, Rényi relative entropies constitute, up to linear combinations, the most general class of relative entropies, naturally motivating the search for their minimal and maximal quantum extensions. The minimal extension is known to be the reverse sandwiched Rényi relative entropy for $α\in[0,1/2)$ and the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy for $α\geq 1/2$. In contrast, the maximal extension had previously been identified only for $α\in[0,2]$, where it is given by the geometric Rényi relative entropy. In this work, we complete this characterization by proving that for $α>2$, the maximal extension is given by the $α$-$z$ Rényi relative entropy with $z=α-1$. As an application, we determine when an energy-incoherent state can be transformed into an energy-coherent state by a Gibbs-preserving operation assisted by an uncorrelated catalyst, thereby fully characterizing the coherence-generating power of this class of operations in the catalytic setting.
summary: This paper fully characterizes the maximal quantum extension of Rényi relative entropies for all parameters $\alpha$, resolving an outstanding problem for $\alpha > 2$. It proves that this maximal divergence is given by a specific form, $D_{\alpha, \alpha-1}(\rho\|\sigma)$. The result has a direct application in quantifying the coherence-generating power of quantum operations.
main_problem: The central problem is to characterize the maximal quantum extension of classical Rényi relative entropies for all parameters $\alpha$, specifically addressing the case where $\alpha > 2$. This completes a characterization previously limited to $\alpha \in [0, 2]$.
main_result: The paper proves that for $\alpha > 2$, the maximal quantum relative entropy is given by the $\alpha-z$ Rényi relative entropy with $z = \alpha-1$. This provides a complete characterization of both minimal and maximal extensions.
method: The authors use techniques involving data-processing inequalities, variational characterizations (finding upper bounds), and establishing lower bounds through constructions involving quantum channels and state preparations to prove the required equalities/inequalities.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on general quantum states ($\rho, \sigma$) defined on a Hilbert space $A$, relating them to classical probability distributions ($p, q$). The framework involves studying various regularized relative entropy divergences (measured and prepared).
key_observables: Rényi relative entropies ($D_\alpha$), minimal/maximal quantum extensions of these entropies, and the coherence-generating power quantified by divergence inequalities.
important_parameters: The parameter $\alpha$ defining the Rényi entropy is crucial, with distinct results found for $\alpha \in [0, 1/2)$, $\alpha \geq 1/2$, $\alpha \in [0, 2]$, and finally $\alpha > 2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the additivity of regularized quantities in the limit $n\to\infty$ and the faithfulness of the relative entropy for all relevant parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates that the maximal relative entropy switches to the form $D_{\alpha, \alpha-1}$ when $\alpha > 2$, confirming the theoretical result.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds the characterization by first reviewing known results for minimal extensions. It then tackles the maximal extension, proving the necessary and sufficient conditions for state transformations (coherence generation) using established inequalities derived from data processing and convexity arguments across different $\alpha$ regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental mathematical tools—the complete characterization of quantum relative entropies—that underpin resource theories in quantum information, which are relevant to understanding coherence measures in open quantum systems dynamics.
